text:
sam: heads up — macOS fastbuild CI is red after the compiler/toolchain bump to clang-15. Failing during link of //src/core:core_lib. Not sure if it's a libc++/libstdc++ mismatch or missing link flag. Job: https://ci.redwood/internal/34567

ci-bot: Job #34567 — macOS-fastbuild — FAILED (linker error)

maya: ugh. can you paste the tail of the linker output?

sam: here's the relevant chunk:
```
Undefined symbols for architecture x86_64:
  "std::__1::mutex::lock()", referenced from:
      xyz::startup() in core_lib.a(startup.o)
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture x86_64
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
```

ev an: wild guess: default stdlib changed to libc++ and some object was built against libstdc++ (or vice versa). Did the toolchain bump change -stdlib default?

alex-ops: +1, I've seen this when the C++ runtime switch wasn't propagated to all toolchains. Also check if the prebuilt third_party .a was compiled on the older ABI.

maya: can we repro locally quick? sam, try `bazel build //src/core --config=macos_fastbuild --sandbox_debug` and then `otool -L bazel-bin/src/core/core_lib` to see which c++ abi it's linked against.

sam: running now. otool shows "@rpath/libc++.1.dylib" for core_lib, but startup.o in core_lib.a references __1 symbols — so libc++ expected. Third_party/util.a is linked against libstdc++ (libstdc++ uses std::__cxx11 mangling).

evan: that confirms mixed ABIs. Quick fixes: 1) rebuild third_party util with libc++ 2) pin the macOS toolchain in CI back to clang-14 until we rebuild 3) add a transitional LDFLAGS to force link against libstdc++ (risky).

sam: option 2 sounds fastest to get green. How do we pin CI toolchain?

maya: you can override the toolchain version in the WORKSPACE for the macos toolchain or set a CI env var that the build matrix reads: e.g., in the buildkite job set MACOS_CLANG_VERSION=14. For bazel's apple toolchain, we have a macos_toolchain_version flag in //ci/config:macos.bzl.

alex-ops: I can push a quick PR that forces the matrix to use clang-14 for the fastbuild job. sample patch:
```diff
diff --git a/ci/pipelines/fastbuild.yml b/ci/pipelines/fastbuild.yml
@@
-    env:
-      MACOS_CLANG_VERSION: 15
+    env:
+      MACOS_CLANG_VERSION: 14  # temporary pin while we rebuild third_party
```

sam: please do that and trigger a canary run on the failing job. I'll also open an internal ticket to rebuild third_party/util with libc++ and add it to the migration checklist.

ci-bot: Buildkite: triggered pipeline fastbuild-canary (#34568) by alex-ops — macOS clang-14

maya: also add a smoke test that verifies no mixed stdlib in the link step (otool check) to prevent reoccurrence.

sam: good call. I'll add the smoke into //ci/tests:link-sanity.

ci-bot: Job #34568 — macOS-fastbuild (canary) — PASSED

sam: ✅ canary green. I'll land the pin PR and queue the full rollout. Follow-up: rebuild third_party with libc++ and then flip the version back. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alex-ops: PR merged and rolled out to fastbuild. Created ticket INFRA-2219 to rebuild third_party/util and track the flip.

maya: leaving notes in the release checklist so the flip isn't accidental.

sam: closing this thread — thanks everyone.
